data.about: A sculpture has to fit under the canopy of task 3, and it does not. So raise the right-hand wall and let the roof hang crooked. Two decisions now instead of one — how high the right wall goes, and how deep the cable hangs — and the two supports stop being equal: the higher one always takes more. Then the cable gets dimensioned for the force that governs, and braced. The defaults are the geometry the course’s own plate draws, Δ = 13.83 m and f = 6.95 m; the forces printed beside it are 2.56 % too large, and this view prints the corrected ones, exactly as ex3_3 does for task 3.

steps.caption: the Creative task: a sculpture has to go under the canopy of task 3 and the roof is too low. Raise the right-hand wall slab, design the new form, dimension the cable, and brace it
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: the load is unchanged from task 3 — the same 37.5 kN/m over the same 65 m. Only the right-hand support is going to move
steps.title: What carries over

steps.caption: left: still q·L through the middle of the span — right: still the whole load line. What changes is where it gets divided
steps.title: The resultant

steps.caption: the first design decision, and the task leaves it free — "choose a new height for the right support wall". The default here is the height the official plate draws. The chord from A to B now tilts, and with it everything else: the roof is no longer symmetric, so the two supports will no longer share the load equally
steps.title: a) Raise the right wall

steps.caption: the second decision, also free, also defaulted to the plate: the parabola hangs 6.95 m below the tilted chord there. Left: the parabola through both supports and its two end tangents — right: those tangents as rays, crossing at the pole. Where the pole sits also decides where the load line divides
steps.title: a) Choose the sag

steps.caption: the load line divides at i, and the two parts are the vertical reactions. They are NOT equal any more: the higher support pulls the harder, because the cable arrives there at the steeper angle
steps.title: a) The two reactions

steps.caption: the steeper end governs, and that is the raised one. This is the force the cable has to be dimensioned for — and it is where this view parts company with the printed answers, for the same reason ex3_3 does on task 3
steps.title: a) The governing force

steps.caption: the same route as EX 2.2: the design strength is the characteristic strength divided by the material factor, the required area is force over strength, and the diameter follows from the area
steps.title: b) The cable diameter

steps.caption: a hanging roof is stiff against the load it was shaped for and floppy against everything else — wind along the building, an unevenly spread snow load. Cross-ties between the cables in the plan turn the row of separate cables into one surface that can share a local load out sideways
steps.title: c) Bracing the roof

data.title: EX 3 Creative — an asymmetric hanging roof
